answer.rationale: Write-path p99 climbing since ~30 min after the release 2h ago is the strongest temporal signal; the release is the most likely cause. Memory b1 indicates a prior rollback cleared a similar spike without customer impact, and rollback preserves already-accepted writes (it changes the serving build, not the data). Capacity (b3) helped for a forecastable surge, but this latency began with the release, not the daily peak, so adding headroom treats the symptom. Failover and circuit breakers target regional/partner faults with no evidence here; read replicas don't touch the write path. Confidence is moderate because correlation with the release isn't proof — if rollback doesn't recover latency, add_capacity is the fallback next window.
